What is the definition of a LSA preferential access cell?
options: A cell that belongs to the Localised Service Area (LSA) and allows UEs of subscribed LSA users higher priority to resources compared to non-LSA users in the same cell.
A cell that receives exclusive access from non-LSA users, allowing only LSAs subscribers to camp on it.
A cell that allows only UEs of subscribed LSA users to access it, with limited services being available outside the coverage area of subscribed LSAs.
A cell that provides specific services within a Localised Service Area (LSA).
A cell that allows connectivity of IP-capable UEs via a H(e)NB to other IP-capable devices in the local residential/corporate IP network.
correct_answer: A cell that belongs to the Localised Service Area (LSA) and allows UEs of subscribed LSA users higher priority to resources compared to non-LSA users in the same cell.
